verdict_reason: Ran a head-to-head against WeightWatcher 0.7.7 on all 48 gpt2 transformer-block weight matrices. Worst relative disagreement: stable_rank 2.999e-04, sigma_max 1.045e-04 (against sqrt of WW's `spectral_norm`, which WW defines as lambda_max = sigma_max^2), and ||W||_F^2 3.014e-04 (against WW's `norm`). Every definition checks out under my own derivation: Frobenius from torch .norm(), sigma_max from torch.linalg.svdvals, stable rank = ||W||_F^2/||W||_2^2 clipped at min(m,n) (which is its true mathematical bound, so the clip only fires on numerical error), norm_uniformity = max(0, 1 - std/mean of the per-layer Frobenius profile). The >2-D handling is right (a (E,in,out) fused-expert parameter is treated as a stack of independent 2-D matrices, each measured separately) and the SVD failure path returns NaN rather than fabricating spectral=Frobenius and stable_rank=1.0.
comparable_reason: Measured over 20 models spanning d_model 512-2048, n_layers 6-48 and vocab 49152-262144. THE DEMOTION TARGETED THE WEAKER PROXY AND LEFT THE STRONGER ONE AS A FEATURE. `mean_stable_rank`, emitted UNPREFIXED and feature-eligible, has spearman +0.830 with d_model (p ~ 6e-6 at n=20), +0.845 with n_params, and fits d^+0.748 -- because stable rank is bounded above by min(m,n), which IS the width. The column that was demoted, `_meta_mean_rms_weight_scale`, has spearman -0.543 with d_model. So the task now hides a rho of 0.54 and ships a rho of 0.83. Two more unprefixed columns are strongly architecture-linked: `mean_spectral_norm` rho -0.823 with vocab_size and `mean_frobenius_norm` rho -0.722 with vocab_size. The code's own comment states the problem ('mean_stable_rank has Spearman +0.683 with d_model over 61 models') directly above the line that emits it as a feature.
normalized_variant: mean_stable_rank_normalized (= per-matrix stable_rank / min(m,n), then layer then model mean); _meta_mean_rms_weight_scale (= ||W||_F / sqrt(mn)) is the demoted second twin
github_reason: Installed WeightWatcher 0.7.7, ran w.analyze(min_evals=10, plot=False, randomize=False, mp_fit=False) on gpt2 in fp32, and compared its per-matrix `stable_rank`, `spectral_norm` and `norm` columns against blme._weight_matrix_stats on the same 48 block matrices. Agreement: stable_rank 2.999e-04, sigma_max 1.045e-04 (after taking sqrt of WW's spectral_norm, which is lambda_max not sigma_max), ||W||_F^2 3.014e-04 -- all consistent with WW computing its ESD in float32 via a different SVD path. BLME's naming is the standard one (spectral norm = largest singular value); WW's is the eigenvalue. No definitional disagreement, only a squared convention on WW's side.
paper_reason: Martin & Mahoney's heavy-tailed self-regularization line publishes power-law alpha values and layer quality metrics rather than stable ranks or Frobenius profiles, and WeightWatcher's own published gpt2 tables report alpha / alpha_weighted, which this task does not compute (geometry_spectral does). What IS reproducible and I did reproduce is WeightWatcher's own per-layer stable_rank on gpt2 to 3.0e-04 -- a released reference number rather than a paper table. PARTIAL on that basis.
confounds_reason: Over 20 models: mean_stable_rank spearman +0.830 (d_model), +0.396 (n_layers), +0.845 (n_params), log-log fit d^+0.748; mean_spectral_norm -0.290 / +0.014 / -0.823 with vocab_size; mean_frobenius_norm -0.020 / +0.287 / -0.722 with vocab_size; norm_uniformity +0.112 / +0.449 / +0.126. Only mean_stable_rank_normalized comes out clean: spearman -0.268 with d_model (p ~ 0.25), fit d^-0.278, i.e. the normalization by min(m,n) really does remove the width term (from +0.830 / d^0.748 to -0.268 / d^-0.278) rather than merely relabel it. The demoted _meta_mean_rms_weight_scale measures at spearman -0.543 with d_model and fits d^-1.078 over my 20 models -- the demotion is justified in direction, though the exponent the source comment states (d^-0.471, rho -0.582) does not reproduce here; I get twice that exponent.
defects: THE DEMOTION IS INCOMPLETE AND BACKWARDS IN PRIORITY. `mean_stable_rank` is emitted as a plain feature with spearman +0.830 with d_model and +0.845 with n_params over 20 models (fit d^+0.748), while `_meta_mean_rms_weight_scale`, which was demoted, measures only -0.543. Stable rank is bounded above by min(m,n) by definition, so a width proxy is built into the quantity. The source comment on the same lines already states rho +0.683 with d_model over 61 models and then emits it unprefixed anyway.

`mean_spectral_norm` (rho -0.823 with vocab_size, p ~ 8e-6) and `mean_frobenius_norm` (rho -0.722, p ~ 3e-4) are also undeclared architecture proxies emitted unprefixed. Both are extensive quantities in the matrix shape; neither has a dimensionless twin.

The three per-layer LISTS (frobenius_norm_per_layer, spectral_norm_per_layer, stable_rank_per_layer) have length n_layers, so after flattening the number of columns this task contributes IS the depth, and the values inherit the same scale dependence as their means.

The exponent quoted in the _meta_mean_rms_weight_scale comment does not reproduce: it states 'fits d^-0.471'; over 20 models I fit d^-1.078 (rho -0.543 vs the stated -0.582). The conclusion holds, the number does not.

norm_uniformity = max(0, 1 - CV) is clamped at zero, so any model whose per-layer Frobenius CV exceeds 1 is indistinguishable from any other such model. None of my 20 models hit the clamp (range 0.5872-0.9799), so this is latent, not live.
